title: Polymarket Hedged Liquidity Rewards Bot
mvp_horizon: MVP is real-data shadow mode; full product is a live hedged four-quote bot

problem.summary: Build a high-performance local-first Rust system for Polymarket that validates and then executes a reward-first, fully hedged binary market-making strategy.
problem.context: The MVP must use real Polymarket data to discover reward-eligible binary markets, compute candidate quotes, compute full-size immediate hedgeability from opposite-outcome depth, and report what would be traded without placing live orders. The full product then adds auth, inventory, live orders, and fill-triggered offsetting hedges.

goals: Use real market data to validate selection, quote math, and hedgeability before live trading.
Trade only binary reward-eligible markets with summed daily rewards of at least 20.
Model four quote legs: YES bid, YES ask, NO bid, NO ask.
Approve quotes only when the full intended fill size is immediately hedgeable using opposite-outcome liquidity.
Prefer passive reward capture and execute a hedge only after a resting order fills.
Persist enough data for audit, replay, and later strategy refinement.
non_goals: Manual market allowlists by type or name as a required filter.
Multi-outcome or negative-risk market making in the first live version.
Dependence on pre-existing external historical order-book archives.

success_metrics.target: 100% of selected markets satisfy daily_reward_total >= 20 and binary reward eligibility
100% of selected quotes pass identity, book, and hedgeability checks before approval
< 50 ms p95 excluding external network latency
< 150 ms p95 excluding external network latency
100% of evaluated markets produce explicit trade/no-trade reasons
0 unresolved incidents beyond configured timeout in normal live operation
success_metrics.notes: Applies after live mode is enabled

personas.name: Owner-Operator
personas.job_to_be_done: Run the bot locally, validate the strategy in shadow mode, then enable live trading with strict controls.
pain_points: Need for high performance with low operational overhead
Need for transparent reasons for trade or no-trade decisions
Need for strict risk controls and kill switches

personas.name: Strategy Researcher
personas.job_to_be_done: Use captured real data to validate the math, improve hedgeability logic, and refine thresholds.
pain_points: No guaranteed documented aggregate market-maker score endpoint
Need visibility into hedgeability and reward-vs-cost logic

in: Public market discovery and reward ingestion
REST bootstrap and WebSocket order-book maintenance
Rules-based market universe using reward threshold
Live mode with auth, inventory, orders, hedging, and kill switches in later phases
out: Manual category or name allowlists as a required selection mechanism
Multi-outcome or negative-risk MM in the first live version
Hosted cloud control plane as a requirement

journeys.name: Shadow discovery and selection
steps: Fetch candidate markets and reward metadata
Filter to binary reward-eligible markets with daily_reward_total >= 20
Reconcile condition IDs, token IDs, outcomes, and reward configuration
Compute quote candidates and full-size hedgeability
Report selected and rejected markets with reasons

journeys.name: Shadow quote evaluation
steps: Maintain YES and NO books from REST plus WebSocket
Compute weighted-average opposite-side hedge cost for full candidate size
edge_cases: Top of book appears sufficient but deeper hedge cost fails
One or more legs are suppressed
Insufficient opposite-outcome depth for full fill size

journeys.name: Live fill and offsetting hedge
steps: Measure deviation from target exposure or inventory
Execute offsetting opposite-outcome hedge if needed
Return to target posture or kill-switch

stories.story: The system MUST discover candidate markets from public Polymarket market surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Given a discovery cycle, when the system runs, then it fetches candidate binary markets and associated reward metadata.
Given a candidate market, when normalized, then it includes condition_id, market_slug, question, outcomes, token IDs, state fields, and reward config if present.
Given a market with more than two outcomes, when evaluated, then it is rejected.

stories.story: The system MUST use a rules-based market universe instead of a manual name or type allowlist.
acceptance_criteria: Given discovered markets, when eligibility is computed, then only binary reward-eligible markets with daily_reward_total >= 20 are included.
Given multiple rewards_daily_rate entries, when evaluated, then the system sums them into daily_reward_total.
Given reward data is missing or malformed, when evaluated, then the market is rejected.

stories.story: The system MUST reconcile one canonical market identity across metadata and book sources.
acceptance_criteria: Given multiple sources, when reconciliation runs, then mismatched condition IDs, token IDs, or outcome labels cause rejection.
Given successful reconciliation, when stored, then one canonical mapping from condition_id to YES and NO token IDs exists.
Given canonical identity changes after admission, when detected, then the market is quarantined.

stories.story: The system MUST bootstrap each YES and NO book from REST before streaming updates.
acceptance_criteria: Given an admitted market, when bootstrap begins, then both YES and NO books are fetched by token ID.
Given a returned book, when normalized, then bids, asks, timestamp, and identifiers are stored.
Given bootstrap fails, when quote evaluation is attempted, then the market remains non-tradable.

stories.story: The system MUST maintain local market state using WebSocket updates with controlled REST resync.
acceptance_criteria: Given subscribed asset IDs, when market updates arrive, then local state is updated atomically.
Given drift or gaps are suspected, when detected, then a REST resync is performed.
Given degraded state, when safety cannot be guaranteed, then quote approval is blocked.

stories.story: The live system MUST ingest authenticated user order and trade events.
acceptance_criteria: Given live mode, when user-channel events arrive, then local order and exposure state is updated.
Given reconnect, when state may be incomplete, then open orders are reconciled.
Given shadow mode, when no trading is enabled, then user-channel ingestion may be disabled.

stories.story: The system MUST model four quote legs per admitted market.
acceptance_criteria: Given a market state, when planning runs, then YES bid, YES ask, NO bid, and NO ask are evaluated.
Given a leg is not viable, when outputs are produced, then a suppression reason is recorded.
Given shadow mode, when asks are modeled, then inventory assumptions are clearly labeled if simulated.

stories.story: The system MUST only approve a quote size that is immediately hedgeable in full using opposite-outcome liquidity.
acceptance_criteria: Given a candidate quote with size q, when hedgeability is computed, then the engine walks opposite-outcome depth until q is satisfied or liquidity is exhausted.
Given sufficient depth, when cost is computed, then weighted-average hedge price, total hedge cost, and slippage are calculated for the full q.
Given insufficient depth or excessive cost, when evaluated, then the quote is rejected or downsized.
Given a shadow report, when displayed, then max_hedgeable_size is included.

stories.story: The system MUST only approve quotes when expected reward opportunity exceeds estimated hedge and execution cost.
acceptance_criteria: Given a candidate quote set, when viability is computed, then reward opportunity, hedge cost, and adverse-selection penalty are estimated.
Given estimated costs exceed configured threshold, when evaluated, then the quote set is rejected.
Given uncertainty is high, when data is insufficient, then the market is downgraded or rejected.

stories.story: The strategy MUST remain passive-first and only hedge after a resting order fills.
acceptance_criteria: Given no fill, when the market remains stable, then the system does not pre-hedge by crossing the spread.
Given a resting order fills, when imbalance appears, then hedge execution is allowed.
Given shadow mode, when reporting occurs, then hedge actions are hypothetical and only modeled after hypothetical fills.

stories.story: The live bot MUST support Polymarket authentication and signed trading requests.
acceptance_criteria: Given live mode, when auth initializes, then API credentials are loaded or derived correctly.
Given authenticated requests are sent, when trading runs, then required auth is attached correctly.
Given auth failure, when detected, then trading does not start.

stories.story: The live bot MUST distinguish owned inventory from external market liquidity.
acceptance_criteria: Given a YES ask, when approval is checked, then owned YES inventory is required or intentionally created.
Given a NO ask, when approval is checked, then owned NO inventory is required or intentionally created.
Given a bid, when approval is checked, then available collateral is required.
Given split or merge support is enabled, when needed, then complete sets may be created or collapsed.
stories.notes: Inventory is owned position state, not book depth

stories.story: The live bot MUST execute an offsetting opposite-outcome hedge when a fill creates unacceptable imbalance.
acceptance_criteria: Given a resting order fill, when exposure or inventory deviates beyond tolerance, then an offsetting hedge intent is created immediately.
Given opposite-outcome liquidity remains available, when the hedge executes, then the system moves back toward target posture.
Given the hedge cannot complete within cost or time limits, when detected, then the market is de-risked or kill-switched.

stories.story: The live bot MUST manage passive limit orders for approved quote intents.
acceptance_criteria: Given approved live quote intents, when execution runs, then orders are submitted as passive limit orders and tracked locally.
Given quote drift exceeds thresholds, when detected, then cancel-replace is used.
Given market disablement, when triggered, then open orders for that market are canceled.

stories.story: The system MUST enforce hard risk controls in both shadow and live modes.
acceptance_criteria: Given stale books, auth failure, identity mismatch, or unresolved drift, when detected, then the market is halted.
Given live mode and unhedged timeout exceeds threshold, when detected, then the market is kill-switched.
Given capital limits are exceeded, when detected, then no new quotes are approved.

stories.story: The system MUST persist market, reward, book, quote, hedgeability, and decision events.
acceptance_criteria: Given any relevant event, when persisted, then event time and ingest time are stored.
Given restart, when recovery runs, then monitored state can be rebuilt from storage plus fresh sync.
Given a finished session, when reviewed, then all selected and rejected markets are reconstructable.

stories.story: The MVP MUST report what the bot would do using real data.
acceptance_criteria: Given an evaluated market, when reporting occurs, then reward total, book summary, candidate quotes, max hedgeable size, estimated hedge cost, and final trade or no-trade decision are output.
Given a rejected market, when reporting occurs, then explicit reasons are output.
Given a hypothetical fill, when simulated, then the offsetting hedge that would be attempted is output.

stories.story: The system SHOULD estimate reward competitiveness locally and calibrate assumptions when possible.
acceptance_criteria: Given local books and reward configuration, when estimation runs, then a local score proxy is computed.
Given per-order scoring checks are available, when sampled, then assumptions are calibrated.
Given aggregate score is not directly documented in reviewed docs, when reporting occurs, then aggregate estimates are labeled approximate.

nonfunctional_requirements.requirement: The system MUST use Rust for latency-sensitive services.
Market-data ingestion from WebSocket event receipt to normalized in-memory state update SHOULD complete in under 100 ms p95 on local hardware, excluding external network latency.
Shadow-mode recomputation after a relevant market event SHOULD complete in under 50 ms p95, excluding external network latency.
Live fill-to-hedge-intent creation SHOULD complete in under 150 ms p95, excluding external network latency.
The system MUST prefer WebSocket-first ingestion over aggressive polling for live data.
Secrets MUST never be written to logs, reports, or crash output.
The system MUST fail closed on auth inconsistency, identity mismatch, or unresolved book drift.
Tracing SHOULD be optional and low-overhead.

analytics.trigger: A candidate market is discovered from public endpoints
A candidate market fails any admission rule
A market passes discovery and validation gates
A four-leg quote model is produced
A candidate quote passes full-size immediate hedgeability
A candidate quote fails full-size immediate hedgeability
A market passes final shadow-mode viability checks
A live fill requires an offsetting hedge

risks.risk: No documented aggregate market-maker score endpoint identified in reviewed docs
risks.mitigation: Use conservative local score proxy and calibrate with per-order scoring checks

risks.risk: Opposite-side liquidity may disappear between evaluation and fill
risks.impact: Live hedge cost may exceed modeled hedge cost
risks.mitigation: Use conservative size caps, slippage caps, and timeout-based kill switches

risks.risk: Four-sided live quoting requires owned inventory for asks
risks.impact: Some modeled quote sets may not be live-deployable without split inventory
risks.mitigation: Separate shadow modeling from live inventory eligibility and support split/merge flows

risks.risk: Excess REST polling may create throttling or degraded recovery behavior
risks.mitigation: Use WebSocket-first runtime and bounded REST resync

open_questions: What exact max hedge-cost rule should gate quote approval?
What exact slippage cap should gate quote approval?
Should asks be fully modeled in shadow mode even when live inventory is not present?
What is the initial per-market capital cap in live mode?
What hedge timeout should trigger a kill switch?
assumptions: Rust provides the best balance of speed, safety, and implementation practicality for this system.
The full product is a live bot, but the MVP is a real-data shadow system.
Markets are selected by reward eligibility and daily reward threshold rather than a manual type or name allowlist.
Only binary markets are targeted in this version.
A quote is valid only if its full fill size is immediately hedgeable using opposite-outcome depth at acceptable cost.
The strategy remains passive-first and only executes a hedge after a fill.
Inventory means owned YES and NO tokens plus collateral, not external market depth.
Historical research begins with data captured by this system.
